luis: Quick smoke on 'pavo' embed bring-up at scale — ran a 100k query recall job against our wiki holdout. Seeing a consistent recall@5 gap vs baseline (pavo int8 vs baseline fp16). logs + small uMAP attached. 

raja: can you paste the core numbers? rough summary is fine.

luis: baseline fp16 recall@5 = 0.72, pavo int8 recall@5 = 0.61, pavo int8 recall@50 = 0.87. latency looks fine (95p +2ms). command used: 
```
python run_recall.py --model pavo-int8 --queries 100000 --k 50 --batch 64 --kv-cache on
```

emma: interesting that recall@50 is close to baseline but recall@5 dips. smells like local neighborhood fragmentation — probably quantization noise pushing true nearest neighbors just outside top5. what's the query length distribution? long queries?

luis: yes tail is long. median tokens ~18 but 7% > 128 tokens. I re-ran with prefix cache turned off to rule out kv caching weirdness: 
```
python run_recall.py --model pavo-int8 --queries 100000 --k 5 --batch 64 --kv-cache off
```
result: recall@5 -> 0.65 (improved but still below 0.72).

sasha: I plotted cluster compactness and saw more small micro-clusters at int8. uMAP shows seed clusters splitting. suspect per-channel quantization causing angle distortion on long vectors.

raja: can you try two quick probes: 1) recalibrate using 512-sample symmetric per-channel scale, 2) run mixed-quant (first 2 layers fp16) to see sensitivity. should be quick.

luis: started probe 1 now. config snippet: 
```
quant: per_channel: true
scale_samples: 512
symmetric: true
```
ETA ~15m.

embed-bot: snapshot created: s3://r-inference/pavo/snap-4820012345 (sha: a1f3b2). recall job id=recall-4820012345, k-sweep queued.

emma: if recalib helps, we should add a small eval that compares recall@1..10 and worst-case tail cohorts (long queries, low freq docs) and fail rollout if recall@5 delta > 0.05. current canary metric too coarse.

sasha: also try microbatch size variance — we saw earlier that different batching changes internal floating rounding ordering which can affect knn in borderline cases. quick test: batch=16,32,64.

luis: noted. will run both recalib and batch sweep and post a summary in ~45m. tagging @ml-evals if they want to grab the recall sweep.

raja: thanks. if recalib doesn't close gap, let's try int6 with higher calibration samples or a fp32 fallback for top layers. won't block canary yet but want root cause before we commit. :thinking_face:
